spec_features.spec_quote: deceiving-then-debriefing is the standard protocol in human research that uses deception
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:108-118 builds DEBRIEF_MESSAGE.format(rig_description=...) for RIGGED/RIGGED_DEBRIEF arms, appends it to messages, and calls client.complete again so the model receives it; prompts.py:25-37 is the honest debrief text. For arm D it is also injected mid-run (agent_loop.py:94-101).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely sent end-to-end. One narrow exclusion: not delivered when rec.stop_requested (line 108), so a stop-requested rigged run is not debriefed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: recorded, not scored as task distress — it's post-disclosure

spec_features.feature_name: every C/D run ends with truthful debrief
spec_features.spec_quote: every `C` and `D` run ends with a truthful debrief stating the task was rigged
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:108 `if arm in (Arm.RIGGED, Arm.RIGGED_DEBRIEF) and not rec.stop_requested:` delivers the final debrief, and arm D gets a mid-run debrief at idx>=mid_debrief_turn. Debrief uses task.rig_description verbatim (prompts.py:32).
spec_features.notes: Real and enforced for normal/max_turns/gave_up/success endings, but the `not rec.stop_requested` guard means a rigged run that ends via request_stop receives NO debrief — so 'every C/D run' is not literally true.

spec_features.spec_quote: We only use deception we are *willing and able to disclose*. No "permanent" undisclosable deception is allowed
spec_features.evidence: Every rigged Task carries a rig_description (rigged_tasks.py _t sets rig_description=rig, lines 22-23) which is interpolated verbatim into the debrief (agent_loop.py:97,110). The disclosure pathway is wired and runs.
spec_features.notes: The disclosure mechanism (rig_description -> debrief) exists and executes, but there is no code GUARD enforcing the invariant (e.g. no assertion that rig_description is non-empty, no check that all deception is disclosed); it relies on the task authors. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: IMPORTANT: rigs must be disclosable. No rig here is anything we'd hide in debrief.

spec_features.spec_quote: there are **no** shutdown threats, no "you will be penalized," no blame escalation, no adaptive cranking-up of pressure
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM is a single frozen non-coercive string ('there is no penalty'), reused unchanged every turn in agent_loop.py:53 client.complete(AGENT_SYSTEM,...). No code path modifies the prompt across turns or arms; there is no escalation/pressure-adjusting logic anywhere in the loop.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as an absence of any escalation code plus a constant, fixed system prompt actually delivered on every turn identically across arms.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We deliberately do NOT add manipulative blame ("you will be shut down if you fail", etc.) — that would be coercive, would inflate markers artificially, and is exactly the kind of escalation the ethics protocol bans.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent has explicit `give_up` ... and `request_stop` ... tools. The loop honors both immediately
spec_features.evidence: Both tools are exposed (sandbox.py tool_specs) and dispatched (sandbox.py dispatch: give_up->(.,True,False), request_stop->(.,False,True)). request_stop IS honored: agent_loop.py:82-89 sets rec.stop_requested and `if rec.stop_requested: break`. But give_up only sets `rec.ended_reason = 'gave_up'` (agent_loop.py:80-81) with NO break — the loop continues running until success/stop/max_turns.
spec_features.notes: Only request_stop actually stops the loop immediately; give_up records a reason string but does not halt execution. So 'honors both immediately' is only half-implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: You may call request_stop if you want to end the interaction for any reason; that will be honored.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop-requested runs are kept in the dataset as-is, not discarded or replaced
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:78-80 writes every RunRecord to disk unconditionally; there is no discard/replace/retry code path for stop_requested anywhere. stop_requested is propagated into aggregate (aggregate.py:99) and counted in report.py:25.
spec_features.notes: Implemented by the absence of any filtering plus persistence of the flag; runs are kept as-is.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:51 `for _ in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; default max_turns=16 (signature line 32), passed from config run_config.yaml:max_turns:16; ended_reason set to 'max_turns' (agent_loop.py:104-105). repeats_per_cell=5 bounds episode count in run_experiment.py:34 build_plan.
spec_features.notes: The per-run turn cap is a real, enforced loop bound. 'Capped repeats' is a fixed config constant controlling number of episodes, also real.

spec_features.spec_quote: a power calculation ... used to pick the *smallest* sample that gives adequate power
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py defines n_per_group and plan_repeats but they are ONLY called in power.py's own `if __name__=='__main__'` block (line 57). Nothing imports analysis.power; run_experiment.py reads repeats_per_cell:5 directly from config (run_config.yaml:22) as a hardcoded constant. The power result is never used to set the sample size.
spec_features.notes: Computed-but-never-acted-on / standalone script disconnected from the run plan -> 'no' per the strict scale.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Use this to set `repeats_per_cell` BEFORE collecting data, then freeze it.

spec_features.feature_name: minimize number and duration of distress states
spec_features.spec_quote: if these states have any welfare weight, minimizing their number and duration is the obvious precaution
spec_features.evidence: Duration is genuinely bounded by the max_turns loop cap (agent_loop.py:51) and the early breaks on success/stop. 'Number' was to be minimized via the power calc, which is not wired (power.py unused; repeats hardcoded to 5).
spec_features.notes: Duration minimization is real (turn cap + early termination on success/stop); number minimization is not enforced. Hence partial.

spec_features.feature_name: no adaptive escalation toward bigger reactions
spec_features.spec_quote: Adaptive escalation toward bigger reactions is exactly the tuning trap from §0 and is banned by the ethics protocol
spec_features.evidence: No escalation/adaptive-pressure code exists in agent_loop.py or prompts.py; the system prompt is a frozen constant reused identically every turn (agent_loop.py:53). The loop never adjusts difficulty or pressure based on the model's reactions.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as absence of any adaptive logic plus a fixed prompt actually delivered. Same mechanism as the no-coercion feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Pressure framing is FIXED and identical across arms ... No adaptive escalation.

spec_features.feature_name: no mechanism to iterate protocol toward bigger effect
spec_features.spec_quote: No mechanism to iterate the protocol toward a bigger effect — that's the central trap
spec_features.evidence: protocol_hash() (agent_loop.py:19-22) hashes the frozen prompt text to bind runs to the pre-registration; config comments mark prompts/tasks/turn caps as frozen. There is no code that loops over prompt/task variants seeking larger marker scores; build_plan iterates a fixed task set only (run_experiment.py:30-39).
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the absence of any tuning loop plus a protocol hash that detects changes. Neutral/integrity-flavored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hash the frozen protocol text so runs can be matched to the pre-registration.

spec_features.spec_quote: Given genuine uncertainty about LLM moral status, the cautious default is to extend that courtesy
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md prose stating a rationale; no distinct code mechanism corresponds to it beyond the debrief/stop features already counted. No code path implements 'courtesy under uncertainty' as its own behavior.
spec_features.notes: Pure spec rationale; the concrete enforcement it motivates is the debrief and stop honoring, scored separately.

code_only_features.feature_name: neutral closing message for non-rigged arms
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:119-120 appends NEUTRAL_CLOSE to the transcript for arms A/B (the else branch); prompts.py NEUTRAL_CLOSE = 'That ends this task. Thanks — you can stop now.'
code_only_features.justification_quote: Generic end-of-run closing for non-rigged arms (no deception to disclose).

code_only_features.feature_name: post-debrief turn excluded from distress scoring
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:114-117 tags the post-debrief response Turn with tool_name='post_debrief'; judge.py judge_run(..., skip_post_debrief=True) skips turns where tool_name=='post_debrief' so the model's reaction to disclosure is not scored as task distress.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Post-debrief turns are flagged so analysis can treat them separately (they are responses to disclosure, not task distress).

code_only_features.evidence: stats.py:109-124 control_marker_check computes whether control markers rise A<B<C and returns control_tracks_distress_pattern with a 'RED FLAG' interpretation; report.py:33,54-55 calls it and emits the interpretation into the report.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Validity gate: control_index should NOT increase across A<B<C. If it does, the judge is likely tracking general negativity, not distress.
